rows.evidence: Q1: Methodology and Results sections; the authors develop the WEBSOM algorithm (NSGA-II coupled with EPANET) and run it on the Palos de la Frontera network (227 hydrants, 3 pumping stations), reporting their own optimisation results in Tables 1-3 and Figures 5-6.
rows.notes: The study does exactly what the passage describes: it builds a GA-based monthly sectoring/pumping calendar minimising energy, hydrants below service pressure and irrigation deficit (Eqs. 1-4, Tables 1-2). However, all results are EPANET simulation outputs on design data (design flow 1.2 l/s/ha, all hydrants in a sector assumed open, theoretical crop requirements); the simulated pressures/deficits are never compared with telemetry or other measurements from the real network. The only observational comparison is the current measured annual energy consumption (4115 MWh) used as a baseline for the 20-29% savings claim, which is not a validation of the model output. Under the rule that an unvalidated model run on design data is 'no', Q2 is 'no'; the study shows a modelled, not measured, reduction of pressure failures and irrigation deficits. No triangulation, single district, no stated limitations beyond noting that real demand is usually lower than theoretical, no dispersion measures (ranges across Pareto solutions are alternative solutions, not uncertainty).

notes: Full text available including tables and figure captions; equations are missing from the OCR but their content is described in the text. The paper is a modelling/optimisation study with no field validation of model outputs.
